title: "08 · Routing"
execute:
  enabled: false
---

A route starts from a coordinate, not from a node, so the first thing that
happens is a snap and the first thing that can be wrong is that snap. Over 500
points the median lands 49.7 m from its nearest intersection, and applied at
both ends that is a median 9.7 % of the trip, 39 % in the worst case measured:
a 582 m route carrying 228 m of pure snapping.

Weighting by travel time instead of distance changes 35 of 200
origin-destination pairs, and where it changes the two routes share only a third
of their edges. The alternatives `k_shortest` returns are a weaker notion than
they sound: the travel-time route appears among them as alternative three of
eight.

The OSMnx router **does** honor the edge weight, unlike the add-on's generic
shortest-path operator, which cannot read one at all and reports a hop count
where you expect meters. The rest of the suite depends on that.
